name: Select Menu Item
summary: One selectable row inside a Select Menu.
description: A single selectable option within a Select Menu, rendered with role="option". Its label is passed as content and a trailing check appears when it is the current selection. It covers the full interaction set — default, hover, focused (keyboard navigation), selected, and disabled — and binds its text, surfaces, and the selected check to the system's semantic tokens.
whenToUse: Represent one choosable option inside a Select Menu listbox
Mark the currently selected value with the trailing check
whenNotToUse: A clickable action or command — use a Menu item, not an option
Standalone outside a Select Menu — items only make sense within the listbox

selected.false: Not the current value — no trailing check.
selected.true: Current value — subtle fill and a trailing brand check.

states.hover: Pointer over the row — subtle background.
states.focused: Keyboard navigation highlight — muted background with a focus ring.

dos: Keep option labels short and scannable
Let the trailing check be the single, consistent selected indicator
Keep items visually uniform within one menu
donts: Don't put multiple interactive controls inside one option row
Don't convey selection by color alone — the check carries it too
Don't use an option row for an action — that belongs in a Menu

keyboard: Reachable via the parent listbox's arrow-key navigation
notes: Carries role="option" with aria-selected reflecting the current value
Disabled options set aria-disabled and leave the tab order
Selection is shown with a check, not color alone (WCAG 1.4.1)
